summary.verdict_reason: Agreement with ChatGPT card appearance is 2/20 (≤12 threshold for rejection). shop.app finds ALL 20 products — it cannot discriminate between products that appear in ChatGPT cards and those that don't. It is not a useful proxy for ChatGPT card appearance.
key_findings: shop.app finds 100% of products searched — it is a product search engine, not a Catalog-syndication filter
The 5 Subimods products (absent from Catalog) ARE found on shop.app — shop.app and the Catalog are different systems with different coverage
shop.app disagrees with Catalog presence on 5/20 (the Subimods products), meeting the ≥5 disagreement threshold, but this is because shop.app is MORE inclusive than the Catalog, not less
Only 2 products appeared in ChatGPT cards, and both were found on shop.app — but so were the other 18 that didn't appear in cards
shop.app presence is necessary but not sufficient for ChatGPT card appearance — every product is on shop.app, but only some appear in cards
implications: shop.app cannot serve as a 'deterministic, cheaply scrapable proxy for Catalog-to-assistant reach' as hypothesized
The hypothesis that shop.app tracks the outcome better than the Catalog API is falsified — shop.app tracks everything, so it tracks nothing specifically
The Catalog API remains the more discriminating instrument: it returns 0 results for Subimods products while shop.app returns 30
The gap between Catalog presence and ChatGPT card appearance is not explained by shop.app presence — it must be explained by something else (ranking, relevance, merchant authority, etc.)
